task: Phase3 S1a request parity comparator (strict TDD)

scaffold.note: test/compare.test.ts was written first; the production file was then a typed API skeleton whose compareRequestTraces returned an empty array. No comparison behavior existed. Missing import was not RED.

positive_tests_that_pass_on_no_op: independent read order and duplicates retained

green_attempt_1.disposition: test-fixture bug, not a production behavior failure: the kind case also changed method from GET to POST, so the implementation correctly reported both kind_mismatch and method_mismatch. The fixture was repaired to keep method/body/dependency equal and change only kind.

test_repair.change: changed-kind case now uses two causal traces with the same method, path, body, and dependency, differing only in kind (mutation vs turn)

red2.note: repaired tests were re-run against the typed empty/no-op scaffold before restoring the implementation

refactor.change: extracted a deterministic finding(code, index, step) constructor and reused it for all findings; no behavior change

followup.change: causal-order finding index is now the original expected event position instead of an indexOf lookup, so duplicate causal labels report an exact index; no behavior change for existing tests

contract.entrypoint: compareRequestTraces(expected: readonly RequestTrace[], actual: readonly RequestTrace[]): readonly TraceDifference[]
contract.identity: expected/actual events are matched by stable `step` labels; volatile `requestId` is present in the model but never compared; duplicated step labels are paired by occurrence count and missing/extra occurrences are reported
contract.reads: independent reads are order-insensitive because list order is never compared; duplicate reads are preserved by occurrence count rather than collapsed
contract.causal: mutation/tool/turn events keep expected causal order and explicit non-null `dependency` labels; pure causal reordering (same step multiset, different sequence) reports one causal_order_mismatch; writes are not sorted by endpoint
contract.canonicalization: method is uppercased; query keys are sorted while repeated-value order is retained; header names are lowercased, headers are grouped/sorted by name while repeated-value order is retained
contract.body: capture-normalized string or null; compared byte-for-byte without trimming or reserialization; never emitted in a finding
contract.auth: authorization/proxy-authorization compare lowercased scheme plus capture-normalized credential; x-api-key/api-key are auth-sensitive; values are never emitted in a finding
contract.findings: deterministic { code, index, step } only; one finding per mismatched field per compared event; no console logging and no throwing on content mismatch

positive: two empty captures return no differences
method case, header case/order, and query key order are canonicalized
independent read order is ignored while duplicate reads are retained
tool/turn dependencies match by stable causal labels
negative: changed non-auth header without leaking value
changed authorization credential without leaking it
missing explicit dependency on a mutation
causal write reorder at the same endpoint
test_coverage.test_style: no mocks; fixtures built independently of the implementation; assertions compare literal { code, index, step } findings

requirement_notes.R12: comparator preserves method/path/query/body/header/status/stream semantics, multiplicity, and causal write/tool/turn order; full client API/refresh work remains S14a
requirement_notes.R14: this slice supplies the pure request comparator and its maintained tests only; React selfcheck, mutation sensitivity, double-run determinism, pixel/ARIA and packaged lanes remain open
requirement_notes.R39: no runtime:verify-client-journeys or runtime:compare-release script is implemented in this slice; root/CI wiring is controller-owned and untouched

limitations: Only the pure request comparator is implemented; no runner, capture normalization, pixel/ARIA comparator, live client lane, or packaged parity is claimed.
packages/ui-parity is not registered in the root workspace/lockfile/CI in this slice; the controller owns those writes and no install/lock change was made.
Auth header comparison assumes the capture supplies a stable, capture-normalized credential (for example a redaction marker or digest); the comparator itself does not redact raw input.
Tests were executed from the package cwd against the root installed vitest/typescript; no fresh install was performed.
The remaining S1 work (runner/selfcheck scripts, scripts/runtime-parity.mjs, verify-client-journeys.mjs, compare-release.mjs, root/CI wiring) stays open.
No commit was created; the controller must perform independent code/test review before acceptance.
